bibliographic.title: Empowering Working Memory for Large Language Model Agents
bibliographic.authors: Jing Guo, Nan Li, Jianchuan Qi, Hang Yang, Ruiqiao Li, Yuzhen Feng, Si Zhang, Ming Xu
bibliographic.citation_apa: Guo, J., Li, N., Qi, J., Yang, H., Li, R., Feng, Y., Zhang, S., & Xu, M. (unclear). Empowering Working Memory for Large Language Model Agents. unclear.

methodology.method_family: cognitive psychology framework application; architectural blueprint
methodology.study_design: conceptual framework proposing Working Memory Hub and Episodic Buffer for LLM agents
methodology.technology_context: large language models, LLM agents, multi-agent systems, ChatGPT as exemplar

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper proposes a working-memory architecture for LLM agents and does not address conversational governance, accountability, compliance, audit, human oversight, or regulated high-stakes deployment contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text discusses LLMs, sequential interactions, dialog episodes, and multi-agent systems, its central focus is cognitive memory architecture (Working Memory Hub, Episodic Buffer) rather than governance of conversational AI. Security is mentioned only as a future research need, with no treatment of risk control, compliance, observability, supervision, or regulated domains. Therefore it falls outside the review scope on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is supported by consistent abstract and introduction content with no governance or regulated-domain signals.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual/architectural proposal without empirical sample, data collection, or evaluated outcomes in the provided text. Appropriate as a design blueprint, but not as empirical evidence for governance practices.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is internally coherent as a memory-architecture proposal, but the provided text offers no empirical validation and little direct relevance to conversational governance or regulated deployment.

coding.subtheme: working memory hub and episodic buffer for cross-episode retention

synthesis.main_claim: LLM agents lack human-like working memory and episodic continuity across dialog episodes; a centralized Working Memory Hub with Episodic Buffer access can improve contextual reasoning in complex and collaborative tasks.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a strategic blueprint for enhancing LLM agent memory by adapting cognitive psychology working-memory frameworks to artificial architectures.
synthesis.limitations: Further research is needed on episodic memory encoding, storage, prioritization, retrieval, and security; human-centric memory concepts may not translate straightforwardly to AI systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems; at most peripheral background on agent memory limitations if needed elsewhere.
